questions.text: स्विद्युत-अपघटनी अपचयन प्रक्रिया द्वारा गलित क्लोराइडों से प्राप्त होने वाली धातुएँ हैं:
questions.text_english: The metals obtained from their molten chlorides by the process of electrolytic reduction are:
questions.solution: The correct answer is (B) Calcium and magnesium. Highly reactive metals like calcium and magnesium cannot be extracted by chemical reduction; they are extracted by electrolytic reduction of their molten chlorides (CaCl₂ and MgCl₂). Gold and silver are noble metals obtained by other processes, aluminium is extracted from its oxide (not chloride) by electrolysis, and iron is obtained by reduction with carbon in a blast furnace.
questions.solution_hindi: सही उत्तर (B) कैल्शियम और मैग्नीशियम है। अत्यधिक क्रियाशील धातुएँ जैसे कैल्शियम और मैग्नीशियम को रासायनिक अपचयन द्वारा नहीं निकाला जा सकता; इन्हें उनके गलित क्लोराइडों (CaCl₂ और MgCl₂) के विद्युत-अपघटनी अपचयन द्वारा प्राप्त किया जाता है।

questions.text: नीचे दिए गए किस विकल्प में मैग्नीशियम ऑक्साइड बनना सही दिखाया गया है?
questions.text_english: The formation of magnesium oxide is correctly shown in option:

options_english.A: Mg transfers 2 electrons to one O → Mg²⁺ [O²⁻]
options_english.B: Mg transfers 1 electron to O → Mg⁺ [O⁻]
options_english.C: Mg transfers 2 electrons to 2 O atoms → Mg²⁺ [O⁻]₂

questions.image_description: Four electron dot structure diagrams (A, B, C, D) showing the transfer of electrons between Mg and O atoms to form magnesium oxide. Option A shows Mg transferring 2 electrons to one O atom forming Mg²⁺ and O²⁻. Option B shows Mg transferring 1 electron forming Mg⁺ and O⁻. Option C shows Mg transferring 1 electron each to two O atoms forming Mg²⁺ and [O⁻]₂. Option D shows 2 Mg atoms each transferring 1 electron to form [Mg²⁺]₂ and O²⁻.
questions.solution: The correct answer is (A). Magnesium has 2 valence electrons and oxygen needs 2 electrons to complete its octet. So one Mg atom transfers both its valence electrons to one O atom, forming Mg²⁺ and O²⁻ ions. The formula of magnesium oxide is MgO. Option B is wrong because Mg loses only 1 electron. Option C incorrectly distributes electrons to two oxygen atoms. Option D incorrectly shows two Mg atoms involved for one O²⁻.
questions.solution_hindi: सही उत्तर (A) है। मैग्नीशियम के 2 संयोजी इलेक्ट्रॉन होते हैं और ऑक्सीजन को अपना अष्टक पूर्ण करने के लिए 2 इलेक्ट्रॉन चाहिए। इसलिए एक Mg परमाणु अपने दोनों संयोजी इलेक्ट्रॉन एक O परमाणु को देता है, जिससे Mg²⁺ और O²⁻ आयन बनते हैं।

questions.text: दो तत्त्वों A और B के बीच अभिक्रिया से कोई यौगिक C बनता है। A इलेक्ट्रॉन खोता है तथा B इलेक्ट्रॉन ग्रहण करता है। यौगिक C निम्नलिखित में से कौन-सा एक गुण नहीं दर्शाएगा?
questions.text_english: Reaction between two elements A and B, forms a compound C. A loses electrons and B gains electrons. Which one of the following properties will not be shown by compound C?

options.B: यह जल में अत्यधिक विलेय है।
options.C: इसके विजातीय (विपरीत आवेशित) आयनों के बीच दुर्बल स्थिर-वैद्युत आकर्षण बल है।
options.D: यह अपनी गलित अवस्था अथवा जलीय विलयन में विद्युत चालन करता है।

options_english.B: It is highly soluble in water.
options_english.C: It has weak electrostatic forces of attraction between its oppositely charged ions.
options_english.D: It conducts electricity in its molten state or aqueous solution.

questions.solution: The correct answer is (C). Compound C is an ionic compound formed by electron transfer. Ionic compounds are characterised by strong electrostatic forces of attraction between oppositely charged ions, not weak forces. Due to these strong forces, ionic compounds have high melting points (A is correct), are generally soluble in water (B is correct), and conduct electricity in molten state or aqueous solution (D is correct). Therefore, option C — which states weak electrostatic forces — is the property that compound C will NOT show.
questions.solution_hindi: सही उत्तर (C) है। यौगिक C एक आयनिक यौगिक है। आयनिक यौगिकों में विपरीत आवेशित आयनों के बीच प्रबल स्थिर-वैद्युत आकर्षण बल होता है, दुर्बल नहीं। इसलिए विकल्प C वह गुण है जो यौगिक C नहीं दर्शाएगा।

questions.text: निम्नलिखित अभिक्रियाओं पर विचार कीजिए: (i) तनु हाइड्रोक्लोरिक अम्ल, सोडियम हाइड्रॉक्साइड से अभिक्रिया करता है। (ii) मैग्नीशियम ऑक्साइड, तनु हाइड्रोक्लोरिक अम्ल से अभिक्रिया करता है। (iii) कार्बन डाइऑक्साइड, सोडियम हाइड्रॉक्साइड से अभिक्रिया करती है। यह पाया जाता है कि प्रत्येक प्रकरण में:
questions.text_english: Consider the following reactions: (i) Dilute hydrochloric acid reacts with sodium hydroxide. (ii) Magnesium oxide reacts with dilute hydrochloric acid. (iii) Carbon dioxide reacts with sodium hydroxide. It is found that in each case:
questions.solution: The correct answer is (A). In all three reactions, salt and water are produced. (i) HCl + NaOH → NaCl + H₂O; (ii) MgO + 2HCl → MgCl₂ + H₂O; (iii) CO₂ + 2NaOH → Na₂CO₃ + H₂O. Option B is incorrect because Na₂CO₃ is a basic salt, not neutral. Option C is wrong because no hydrogen gas is evolved in any of these reactions. Option D is wrong because acidic salts are not formed in all three cases.
questions.solution_hindi: सही उत्तर (A) है। तीनों अभिक्रियाओं में लवण और जल बनते हैं।

questions.text: दन्तवल्क (दन्त इनैमल) कैल्शियम हाइड्रॉक्सीएपेटाइट (कैल्शियम फॉस्फेट का क्रिस्टलीय रूप) से बना होता है। मुख में pH कितना होने पर इस रसायन का संक्षारण आरम्भ हो जाता है?
questions.text_english: Tooth enamel is made up of calcium hydroxyapatite (a crystalline form of calcium phosphate). This chemical starts corroding in the mouth when the pH is:
questions.solution: The correct answer is (B) 5. Tooth enamel starts corroding when the pH in the mouth falls below 5.5. When bacteria in the mouth break down sugar and food particles, they produce acids that lower the pH. At a pH of 5 or below, the acidic environment is strong enough to dissolve and corrode the calcium hydroxyapatite of tooth enamel. A pH of 7 is neutral and does not cause corrosion; pH 10 and 14 are alkaline and would not cause acid corrosion.
questions.solution_hindi: सही उत्तर (B) 5 है। जब मुख में pH 5.5 से नीचे गिर जाता है तो दन्त इनैमल का संक्षारण शुरू हो जाता है।

questions.text: वायु की उपस्थिति में ऐलुमिनियम और मैग्नीशियम के दहन होने पर बनने वाले उत्पाद क्रमश: हैं:
questions.text_english: The products formed when Aluminium and Magnesium are burnt in the presence of air respectively are:
questions.solution: The correct answer is (B) Al₂O₃ and MgO. When aluminium burns in air, it forms aluminium oxide: 4Al + 3O₂ → 2Al₂O₃. Aluminium has a valency of 3 and oxygen has a valency of 2, so the correct formula is Al₂O₃. When magnesium burns in air, it forms magnesium oxide: 2Mg + O₂ → 2MgO. Magnesium has a valency of 2 matching oxygen's valency of 2, giving MgO. All other options contain incorrectly balanced formulae.
questions.solution_hindi: सही उत्तर (B) Al₂O₃ और MgO है। ऐलुमिनियम का दहन: 4Al + 3O₂ → 2Al₂O₃ तथा मैग्नीशियम का दहन: 2Mg + O₂ → 2MgO।

questions.text: जल का विद्युत-अपघटन एक वियोजन (अपघटन) अभिक्रिया है। जल के विद्युत-अपघटन के समय इलेक्ट्रोडों पर मुक्त गैसों – हाइड्रोजन और ऑक्सीजन के द्रव्यमानों का अनुपात (M_H : M_O) होता है:
questions.text_english: Electrolysis of water is a decomposition reaction. The mass ratio (M_H : M_O) of hydrogen and oxygen gases liberated at the electrodes during electrolysis of water is:
questions.solution: The correct answer is (D) 1 : 8. The electrolysis of water produces hydrogen and oxygen in a volume ratio of 2:1, but the question asks for mass ratio. Mass of H₂ produced = 2 × 2 = 4 g (for every 2 moles H₂), mass of O₂ = 1 × 32 = 32 g. So the mass ratio M_H : M_O = 4 : 32 = 1 : 8. Option B (2:1) gives the volume ratio, not mass ratio. Therefore D is correct.
questions.solution_hindi: सही उत्तर (D) 1:8 है। जल के विद्युत-अपघटन से H₂ और O₂ आयतन अनुपात 2:1 में बनती हैं, परन्तु द्रव्यमान अनुपात = 4:32 = 1:8 होता है।

questions.text: निम्नलिखित ग्लूकोज़ के विखण्डन का पथ दर्शाया गया है: ग्लूकोज़ →(a) पायरुवेट + ऊर्जा →(b) लैक्टिक अम्ल + ऊर्जा। स्थल 'a' और 'b' क्रमश: हैं:
questions.text_english: The breakdown of glucose has taken the following pathway: Glucose →(a) Pyruvate + Energy →(b) Lactic acid + Energy. The sites 'a' and 'b' respectively are:

options.A: माइटोकॉन्ड्रिया और ऑक्सीजन के अभाव वाली पेशीय कोशिकाएँ
options.B: कोशिकाद्रव्य और ऑक्सीजन प्रचुर पेशीय कोशिकाएँ
options.D: कोशिकाद्रव्य और ऑक्सीजन के अभाव वाली पेशीय कोशिकाएँ

options_english.A: Mitochondria and Oxygen deficient muscle cells
options_english.B: Cytoplasm and Oxygen rich muscle cells
options_english.D: Cytoplasm and Oxygen deficient muscle cells

questions.solution: The correct answer is (D). Glycolysis — the breakdown of glucose to pyruvate — occurs in the cytoplasm of all cells (site 'a'). The subsequent conversion of pyruvate to lactic acid is anaerobic fermentation that occurs in oxygen-deficient muscle cells during intense exercise (site 'b'). Yeast cells convert pyruvate to ethanol, not lactic acid, so option C is wrong. Mitochondria are the site of aerobic respiration (Krebs cycle), not glycolysis, ruling out option A.
questions.solution_hindi: सही उत्तर (D) है। ग्लाइकोलिसिस (ग्लूकोज़ से पायरुवेट) कोशिकाद्रव्य में होती है (स्थल 'a') और लैक्टिक अम्ल का निर्माण ऑक्सीजन-रहित पेशीय कोशिकाओं में होता है (स्थल 'b')।

questions.text: गोल और हरे (RRyy) बीजों वाले मटर के पौधों का झुर्रीदार और पीले (rrYY) बीजों वाले मटर के पौधों के साथ संकरण कराया गया। F₁ संतति के पौधों द्वारा विकसित बीज होंगे:
questions.text_english: If pea plants with round and green seeds (RRyy) are crossed with pea plants having wrinkled and yellow seeds (rrYY), the seeds developed by the plants of F₁ generation will be:
questions.solution: The correct answer is (C) 100% round and yellow. The cross is RRyy × rrYY. All F₁ offspring will have the genotype RrYy. Since R (round) is dominant over r (wrinkled) and Y (yellow) is dominant over y (green), all F₁ plants will show the dominant phenotype for both traits — round shape and yellow colour. Therefore 100% of the seeds in F₁ generation will be round and yellow.
questions.solution_hindi: सही उत्तर (C) 100% गोल और पीले है। RRyy × rrYY के F₁ में सभी RrYy होंगे। R (गोल) और Y (पीला) दोनों प्रभावी हैं, अतः सभी बीज गोल और पीले होंगे।
questions.topic: Mendel's Laws of Inheritance - Dihybrid Cross

questions.text: उभयलिंगी पुष्प के विषय में सही कथन है/हैं: (i) इनमें पुंकेसर और स्त्रीकेसर दोनों होते हैं। (ii) इनमें या तो पुंकेसर होता है अथवा स्त्रीकेसर होता है। (iii) ये या तो स्वपरागण दर्शाते हैं अथवा परपरागण दर्शाते हैं। (iv) ये अपने आप फल उत्पन्न नहीं कर सकते हैं।
questions.text_english: The correct/true statement(s) for a bisexual flower is/are: (i) They possess both stamen and pistil. (ii) They possess either stamen or pistil. (iii) They exhibit either self-pollination or cross-pollination. (iv) They cannot produce fruits on their own.
questions.solution: The correct answer is (C) — statements (i) and (iii) are correct. A bisexual (hermaphrodite) flower possesses both stamen (male reproductive organ) and pistil (female reproductive organ) in the same flower, making statement (i) correct. Since bisexual flowers have both organs, they can undergo either self-pollination (pollen transferred to the same flower's stigma) or cross-pollination (pollen transferred to another flower), making statement (iii) correct. Statement (ii) is wrong because it describes unisexual flowers. Statement (iv) is wrong because bisexual flowers can produce fruits on their own through self-pollination.
questions.solution_hindi: सही उत्तर (C) है। कथन (i) — उभयलिंगी पुष्प में पुंकेसर और स्त्रीकेसर दोनों होते हैं, यह सत्य है। कथन (iii) — ये स्वपरागण और परपरागण दोनों दर्शा सकते हैं, यह भी सत्य है।

questions.text: वह कौन-सा पादप हॉर्मोन है जिसकी सान्द्रता, प्ररोह के प्रकाश से दूर वाले भाग की कोशिकाओं को लम्बाई में वृद्धि के लिए उद्दीपित करती है?
questions.text_english: The plant hormone whose concentration stimulates the cells to grow longer on the side of the shoot which is away from light is:
questions.solution: The correct answer is (D) Auxins. Auxin is the plant hormone responsible for phototropism. When light falls on one side of a shoot, auxin migrates to the shaded (away from light) side, where it accumulates in greater concentration. This higher concentration of auxin stimulates the cells on the shaded side to elongate more, causing the shoot to bend towards the light. Cytokinins promote cell division, gibberellins promote stem elongation overall, and adrenaline is an animal hormone, not a plant hormone.
questions.solution_hindi: सही उत्तर (D) ऑक्सिन है। ऑक्सिन प्रकाशानुवर्तन के लिए उत्तरदायी पादप हॉर्मोन है। यह प्रकाश से दूर वाले पार्श्व में एकत्रित होकर उन कोशिकाओं को अधिक लम्बा करता है।

questions.text: मुँह में लार का कम मात्रा में स्रावित होना किस परिवर्तन को प्रभावित करेगा?
questions.text_english: Secretion of less saliva in mouth will effect the conversion of:

options.B: वसा से वसीय अम्ल और ग्लिसरॉल

options_english.B: fats into fatty acids and glycerol

questions.solution: The correct answer is (C) starch into simple sugars. Saliva contains the enzyme salivary amylase (ptyalin) which begins the digestion of starch in the mouth, converting it into simpler sugars (maltose). If less saliva is secreted, the activity of salivary amylase is reduced, thus affecting the conversion of starch into simple sugars. Protein digestion begins in the stomach (pepsin), fat digestion in the small intestine (lipase), and alcohol formation is not a digestive process in the body.
questions.solution_hindi: सही उत्तर (C) स्टार्च से सरल शर्करा है। लार में टायलिन (एमाइलेज) एंजाइम होता है जो स्टार्च को माल्टोज में परिवर्तित करता है। कम लार स्रावित होने पर यह प्रक्रिया प्रभावित होगी।

questions.text: किसी स्थलीय पारितंत्र में हरे पादपों की पत्तियों द्वारा प्राप्त सौर ऊर्जा का लगभग कितने प्रतिशत भाग खाद्य ऊर्जा में परिवर्तित नहीं होता है?
questions.text_english: The percentage of solar energy which is not converted into food energy by the leaves of green plants in a terrestrial ecosystem is about:
questions.solution: The correct answer is (D) 99%. Green plants (producers) are able to capture and convert only about 1% of the incident solar energy into food energy (chemical energy) through photosynthesis. The remaining 99% of solar energy is not converted into food energy — it is reflected, transmitted, or lost as heat. This very low efficiency of energy capture is why food chains are short and energy decreases at each trophic level.
questions.solution_hindi: सही उत्तर (D) 99% है। हरे पादप सौर ऊर्जा का केवल लगभग 1% भाग ही खाद्य ऊर्जा में परिवर्तित कर पाते हैं। शेष 99% परिवर्तित नहीं होता।

questions.text: निम्नलिखित में से कौन-कौन से समूह कोई आहार श्रृंखला नहीं बनाते हैं? (i) लेड्या, खरगोश, घास, शेर (ii) प्लवक, मानव, टिड्डा, मछली (iii) बाज़, घास, सर्प, टिड्डा, मेंढक (iv) घास, सर्प, लेड्या, बाघ
questions.text_english: Which of the following groups do not constitute a food chain? (i) Wolf, rabbit, grass, lion (ii) Plankton, man, grasshopper, fish (iii) Hawk, grass, snake, grasshopper, frog (iv) Grass, snake, wolf, tiger
questions.solution: The correct answer is (C) — groups (ii) and (iii) do not form valid food chains. In group (ii), the correct order should be Plankton → Grasshopper → Fish → Man, but the given order (Plankton, Man, Grasshopper, Fish) is incorrect and does not reflect a realistic feeding sequence. In group (iii), Hawk is placed at the beginning before Grass, but in a valid food chain, grass (producer) must come first; the correct order would be Grass → Grasshopper → Frog → Snake → Hawk. Groups (i) and (iv) form valid food chains: Grass → Rabbit → Wolf → Lion and Grass → Snake → Wolf → Tiger respectively.
questions.solution_hindi: सही उत्तर (C) है। समूह (ii) और (iii) वैध आहार श्रृंखला नहीं बनाते क्योंकि इनमें क्रम गलत है।

questions.text: वह कौन-सी परिघटना है जो धुएँ से भरे कमरे में किसी पतले छिद्र से सूर्य के प्रकाश पुंज के प्रवेश करने पर धुएँ के कणों को दृष्टिगोचर बनाने के लिए उत्तरदायी होती है?
questions.text_english: The phenomenon responsible for making the smoke particles visible when a beam of sunlight enters a smoke filled room through a narrow hole is:
questions.solution: The correct answer is (A) scattering of light. When a beam of sunlight enters a dark, smoke-filled room through a narrow hole, the colloidal smoke particles scatter the light in all directions — this is the Tyndall effect. This scattering makes the path of light visible and the smoke particles appear bright. Dispersion refers to splitting of light into its component colours, regular reflection requires smooth surfaces, and total internal reflection occurs at interfaces when light travels from denser to rarer medium — none of these apply here.
questions.solution_hindi: सही उत्तर (A) प्रकाश का प्रकीर्णन है। यह टिन्डल प्रभाव है जिसमें धुएँ के कण प्रकाश का प्रकीर्णन करते हैं जिससे प्रकाश पुंज दृश्य हो जाता है।

questions.text: दर्पण 'X' सूर्य के प्रकाश को सौर भट्टी में संकेंद्रित करता है तथा दर्पण 'Y' वाहनों के पार्श्व में ड्राइवरों को पीछे के ट्रैफिक को देखने के लिए लगाया जाता है। इन दो दर्पणों के विषय में निम्नलिखित में से कौन-से कथन सही हैं? questions.text_english: An object is placed at a distance of 10 cm in front of a concave mirror of focal length 15 cm. Use mirror formula to determine the position of the image formed by this mirror.

key_points: Using mirror formula: 1/v + 1/u = 1/f
u = -10 cm, f = -15 cm (concave mirror, sign convention)
v = +30 cm — image is virtual, behind the mirror

questions.solution: Given: Object distance u = -10 cm (object in front of mirror), focal length f = -15 cm (concave mirror). Using the mirror formula: 1/v + 1/u = 1/f. Substituting values: 1/v + 1/(-10) = 1/(-15). Therefore, 1/v = -1/15 + 1/10 = (-2 + 3)/30 = 1/30. So v = +30 cm. The positive sign indicates that the image is formed 30 cm behind the mirror (on the same side as the object's back). The image is virtual, erect, and magnified.

sub_questions.solution: It is essential to plug leaks in blood vessels not only to prevent blood loss but also to prevent microorganisms and pathogens from entering the body through the wound, which could cause serious infections. questions.text_english: Translate the following statements into chemical equations and then balance them: (a) Nitric acid reacts with calcium hydroxide to form calcium nitrate and water. (b) Sodium chloride reacts with silver nitrate to form silver chloride and sodium nitrate.

key_points: (a) 2HNO₃ + Ca(OH)₂ → Ca(NO₃)₂ + 2H₂O
(b) NaCl + AgNO₃ → AgCl + NaNO₃

questions.solution: (a) Nitric acid reacting with calcium hydroxide: The unbalanced equation is HNO₃ + Ca(OH)₂ → Ca(NO₃)₂ + H₂O. Balancing: calcium has 1 atom on each side, nitrogen needs 2 (to balance 2 NO₃⁻ groups), and hydrogen needs 2 water molecules. Balanced equation: 2HNO₃ + Ca(OH)₂ → Ca(NO₃)₂ + 2H₂O. (b) Sodium chloride reacting with silver nitrate: NaCl + AgNO₃ → AgCl↓ + NaNO₃. This equation is already balanced with 1 atom of each element on both sides. Silver chloride precipitates (white precipitate).

key_points: (a) Parallel resistance of 10Ω and 15Ω: 1/R_p = 1/10 + 1/15 = 3/30 + 2/30 = 5/30; R_p = 6 Ω. Series resistance of 60Ω and 40Ω: R_s2 = 60 + 40 = 100 Ω. Total: R = 6 + 100 = 106 Ω

questions.solution: (a) The 10 Ω and 15 Ω resistors are in parallel: 1/R_p = 1/10 + 1/15 = (3+2)/30 = 5/30, so R_p = 6 Ω. (c) Potential difference across the 10 Ω and 15 Ω parallel combination: V = I × R_p = 0.5 × 6 = 3 V.

questions.text_english: Draw ray diagrams to show the nature, position and relative size of the image formed by a convex mirror when the object is placed (i) at infinity and (ii) between infinity and pole P of the mirror.

key_points: (i) Object at infinity: image forms at principal focus F, behind the mirror; image is virtual, erect, and highly diminished (point-sized)
(ii) Object between infinity and P: image forms between F and P, behind the mirror; image is virtual, erect, and diminished

questions.image_description: Two ray diagrams for a convex mirror: (i) Object at infinity — parallel rays fall on the mirror and after reflection diverge such that they appear to come from the principal focus F behind the mirror. Image is at F, virtual, erect, point-sized. (ii) Object between infinity and pole P — two rays drawn: one parallel to principal axis (reflects as if coming from F), and one directed towards the centre of curvature C (reflects back along same path). The reflected rays diverge and when extended behind mirror, meet between F and P to form virtual, erect, diminished image.
questions.solution: For a convex mirror: (i) When the object is at infinity, incident rays are parallel to the principal axis. After reflection from the convex mirror, the rays diverge and appear to come from the principal focus F located behind the mirror. The image is formed at F, is virtual, erect, and highly diminished (point-sized). (ii) When the object is placed between infinity and the pole P, two standard rays are used — one parallel to principal axis (reflects as if from F) and one aimed at the centre of curvature C. The reflected diverging rays, when extended backward, meet between F and P behind the mirror. The image is virtual, erect, and diminished. In both cases, the image is always virtual and erect for a convex mirror.
questions.solution_hindi: उत्तल दर्पण के लिए: (i) अनंत पर बिम्ब — प्रतिबिम्ब F पर, आभासी, सीधा, बिन्दुआकार। (ii) P और अनंत के बीच बिम्ब — प्रतिबिम्ब F और P के बीच, आभासी, सीधा, छोटा।

Out of these, 2 are sex chromosomes (XX in females, XY in males)

sub_questions.solution: Human beings have 46 chromosomes arranged in 23 pairs in every somatic (body) cell. Out of these 46 chromosomes, 44 are autosomes (22 pairs) and 2 are sex chromosomes (1 pair). In females, the sex chromosomes are XX, while in males they are XY.

sub_questions.text_english: (b) Explain how, in sexually reproducing organisms, the number of chromosomes in the progeny is maintained.

key_points: Gametes (sperm and egg) are formed by meiosis, which halves the chromosome number (haploid — n)
During fertilisation, male gamete (n) fuses with female gamete (n) to form a zygote (2n)
This restores the original diploid chromosome number in the offspring

sub_questions.solution: In sexually reproducing organisms, gametes (sperm and egg cells) are produced through meiosis, a special type of cell division. Meiosis halves the chromosome number, so each gamete is haploid (n = 23 chromosomes in humans). During fertilisation, the male gamete (sperm) fuses with the female gamete (egg) to form a zygote. The zygote thus receives one set of chromosomes from each parent, restoring the diploid number (2n = 46). This ensures that the chromosome number remains constant in every generation of sexually reproducing organisms.

questions.text_english: A hormone 'X' is secreted in blood when a person is under scary situation. (a) Identify the hormone 'X' and the gland that secretes it. (b) Explain its role in dealing with scary or emergency situations.

key_points: (a) Hormone X is Adrenaline (Epinephrine), secreted by the adrenal glands (located on top of kidneys)

(b) Adrenaline increases heart rate, breathing rate, and blood pressure; directs more blood to muscles and brain; increases blood sugar by breaking down glycogen; dilates pupils — prepares body for 'fight or flight' response

questions.solution: (a) Hormone 'X' is Adrenaline (also called Epinephrine). It is secreted by the adrenal glands, which are located at the top of each kidney. (b) When a person faces a scary or emergency situation, adrenaline is rapidly released into the bloodstream. It acts as an emergency hormone by: increasing the heart rate and breathing rate to supply more oxygen to muscles; raising blood pressure and dilating blood vessels to muscles; breaking down glycogen to release glucose for instant energy; dilating the pupils for better vision; and reducing blood supply to the digestive system. All these actions prepare the body for a rapid 'fight or flight' response to overcome the danger.

sub_questions.solution: Activity: Take three test tubes each containing an iron nail. In test tube 1, keep the nail with some water (exposing it to moist air). sub_questions.text_english: (a) 'Displacement reactions also play a key role in extracting metals in the middle of the reactivity series.' Justify this statement with two examples. (b) Why can metals high up in the reactivity series not be obtained by reduction of their oxides by carbon?

key_points: (a) Example 1: Iron extracted by coke in blast furnace (Fe₂O₃ + 3CO → 2Fe + 3CO₂); Example 2: Copper extracted by iron displacement (Fe + CuSO₄ → FeSO₄ + Cu) or zinc from ZnO by carbon
(b) Metals high in the reactivity series (Na, K, Ca, Mg, Al) are more reactive than carbon; carbon cannot displace them from their oxides; they require electrolytic reduction

sub_questions.solution: (a) Metals in the middle of the reactivity series (like iron, zinc, copper) can be extracted using displacement reactions. Example 1: Iron is extracted from its oxide (Fe₂O₃) by reduction with carbon (coke) in a blast furnace: Fe₂O₃ + 3C → 2Fe + 3CO₂. Here, carbon displaces iron. Example 2: Copper can be obtained by adding iron to a copper sulphate solution: Fe + CuSO₄ → FeSO₄ + Cu. Iron, being more reactive, displaces copper. (b) Metals that are high in the reactivity series, such as sodium, potassium, calcium, magnesium, and aluminium, are more reactive than carbon itself. Carbon cannot reduce their oxides because it is not reactive enough to displace these highly reactive metals. Therefore, they must be extracted by electrolytic reduction of their molten ores.

key_points: Negative power indicates a concave (diverging) lens

sub_questions.solution: The power of lens X is –2.5 D. Since the power is negative, lens X is a concave (diverging) lens. The focal length is calculated as: f = 1/P = 1/(–2.5) = –0.4 m = –40 cm. sub_questions.text: (ii) ''किसी लेंस के लिए आवर्धन 'm' का मान –2 है।'' नई कार्तीय चिह्न परिपाटी का उपयोग करते हुए और यह मानते हुए कि कोई बिम्ब इस लेंस के प्रकाशिक केन्द्र से 20 cm की दूरी पर है, निम्नलिखित का उल्लेख कीजिए: (I) बनने वाले प्रतिबिम्ब की प्रकृति; (II) बिम्ब के साइज़ की तुलना में प्रतिबिम्ब का साइज़; (III) प्रतिबिम्ब की स्थिति, तथा (IV) प्रतिबिम्ब की ऊँचाई का चिह्न।
sub_questions.text_english: (ii) 'The value of magnification m for a lens is –2.' Using new Cartesian Sign Convention and considering that an object is placed at a distance of 20 cm from the optical centre of this lens, state: (I) the nature of the image formed; (II) size of the image compared to the size of the object; (III) position of the image, and (IV) sign of the height of the image.

key_points: (I) Real and inverted image (negative magnification means real and inverted for a convex lens)
(II) Image is twice the size of the object (|m| = 2)
(III) m = v/u = -2; u = -20 cm; v = -2 × (-20) = +40 cm (image is 40 cm on the other side of the lens)
(IV) Height of image is negative (inverted)

sub_questions.solution: Given: magnification m = –2, object distance u = –20 cm (using sign convention, object on left). (I) Since the magnification is negative for a lens, the image is real and inverted. (II) |m| = 2, meaning the image is twice the size of the object — it is magnified. (III) Using m = v/u: –2 = v/(–20), so v = +40 cm. The image is formed 40 cm on the other side (right side) of the lens. (IV) Since the image is inverted, the height of the image is negative (the image height has a negative sign, meaning it is below the principal axis).

Power = 1/f; shorter focal length = higher power = greater ability to converge or diverge light

sub_questions.solution: Lens A with focal length 10 cm will show a higher degree of convergence or divergence. This is because the power of a lens is given by P = 1/f (in metres). For lens A: P = 1/0.10 = 10 D. For lens B: P = 1/0.20 = 5 D. A higher power value means the lens can bend (converge or diverge) light rays more strongly. Since lens A has a shorter focal length and therefore greater power, it shows a higher degree of convergence (if convex) or divergence (if concave) compared to lens B.

sub_questions.text_english: (i) Draw a ray diagram to show the refraction of a ray of light through a rectangular glass slab when it falls obliquely from air into glass.

key_points: Ray bends towards normal when entering glass (denser medium)
Ray bends away from normal when exiting glass back to air
Emergent ray is parallel to incident ray but laterally displaced

sub_questions.solution: A ray diagram must show: an incident ray striking the first surface of the glass slab obliquely, with the normal drawn at the point of incidence. The ray bends towards the normal as it enters the denser glass medium (angle of refraction < angle of incidence). Inside the slab, the refracted ray travels in a straight line. At the second surface, the ray bends away from the normal as it exits into the less dense air (angle of refraction > angle of incidence). The final emergent ray is parallel to the original incident ray but is laterally displaced. The angle of incidence equals the angle of emergence.

key_points: The ratio of sine of angle of incidence to sine of angle of refraction is constant for a given pair of media: sin i / sin r = constant (n)
The incident ray, refracted ray, and normal at the point of incidence all lie in the same plane

sub_questions.solution: Snell's Law of Refraction states: (1) The incident ray, the refracted ray, and the normal to the surface at the point of incidence all lie in the same plane. (2) The ratio of the sine of the angle of incidence (i) to the sine of the angle of refraction (r) is a constant for a given pair of media at a given wavelength. This constant is called the refractive index (n) of the second medium with respect to the first: sin i / sin r = n₂₁ = constant.

key_points: (I) Object distance: Convex lens forms virtual image when object is between F and O (within focal length); Concave lens always forms virtual image regardless of object position
(II) Magnification: Convex lens virtual image has magnification > 1 (enlarged); Concave lens virtual image always has magnification < 1 (diminished)

sub_questions.solution: Virtual images formed by a convex lens and a concave lens differ as follows. (I) Object distance: A convex (converging) lens forms a virtual image only when the object is placed between the optical centre O and the principal focus F (i.e., object distance is less than the focal length). A concave (diverging) lens always forms a virtual image for any position of the object. (II) Magnification: The virtual image formed by a convex lens has a magnification greater than 1 (the image is enlarged and erect). The virtual image formed by a concave lens always has a magnification less than 1 (the image is diminished and erect).

(II) Fallopian tube: site of fertilisation; carries the egg/zygote from ovary to uterus
(III) Uterus: site of implantation and development of the embryo/foetus during pregnancy

sub_questions.solution: (I) Ovary: The ovaries produce and release eggs (ova) during ovulation. They also secrete female sex hormones — oestrogen and progesterone — which regulate the menstrual cycle and secondary sexual characteristics. (II) Fallopian tube (oviduct): The fallopian tube carries the released egg from the ovary towards the uterus. It is also the site where fertilisation of the egg by the sperm usually takes place. (III) Uterus: The uterus is a pear-shaped muscular organ where the fertilised egg (zygote) implants and develops into an embryo and then a foetus during the nine months of pregnancy. It provides nourishment and protection to the developing foetus.

sub_questions.text: (ii) पुरुषों (मानव नरों) द्वारा उपयोग की जाने वाली दो गर्भनिरोधक विधियों का संक्षेप में उल्लेख कीजिए।
sub_questions.text_english: (ii) State briefly two contraceptive methods used by human males.

key_points: Condom: a physical/barrier method that prevents sperm from reaching the egg
Vasectomy: a surgical method where the vas deferens is cut and tied to prevent sperm from being released during ejaculation

sub_questions.solution: Two contraceptive methods used by human males are: (1) Condom — This is a physical (barrier) method. A thin sheath (usually made of rubber/latex) is worn over the penis during intercourse. It prevents sperm from entering the female reproductive tract, thereby preventing fertilisation. It also protects against sexually transmitted infections (STIs). (2) Vasectomy — This is a permanent surgical contraceptive method. The vas deferens (the tube that carries sperm from the testes) is surgically cut and tied (ligated). This prevents sperm from being released during ejaculation, making the male permanently infertile.

sub_questions.text_english: (i) Differentiate between self-pollination and cross-pollination.

key_points: Self-pollination: pollen from the anther of a flower reaches the stigma of the same flower or another flower on the same plant; no external agent needed

Cross-pollination: pollen from the anther of a flower of one plant is transferred to the stigma of a flower on a different plant of the same species; requires external agents like wind, insects, or water

sub_questions.solution: Self-pollination occurs when pollen grains from the anther of a flower are transferred to the stigma of the same flower, or to another flower on the same plant. It does not require any external pollinating agent and produces offspring genetically similar to the parent. Cross-pollination occurs when pollen grains from the anther of a flower on one plant are transferred to the stigma of a flower on a genetically different plant of the same species. It requires external agents such as wind, insects, water, or birds, and results in offspring with greater genetic variation and vigour.

sub_questions.text_english: (i) Draw electron dot structure of chlorine molecule. (Atomic Number of Chlorine = 17)

key_points: Cl has 7 valence electrons (electronic configuration 2,8,7)
Two Cl atoms share one electron each to form a single covalent bond (Cl:Cl with 3 lone pairs on each Cl)
Each Cl has 3 lone pairs and 1 shared pair = 8 electrons around each Cl (octet satisfied)

sub_questions.solution: Chlorine (Cl) has atomic number 17 and electronic configuration 2, 8, 7. It has 7 valence electrons. Each chlorine atom needs 1 more electron to complete its octet. In a chlorine molecule (Cl₂), each Cl atom contributes 1 electron to form a shared pair (single covalent bond). Each Cl atom has 3 lone pairs (6 electrons) and shares 1 pair with the other Cl atom. The electron dot structure shows: [:Cl — Cl:] with 3 dots on each side of each Cl atom, and the shared pair represented between them. Both chlorine atoms have a complete octet of 8 electrons.

sub_questions.text_english: (ii) What happens when chlorine reacts with methane in the presence of sunlight? Write the name of the reaction.

key_points: CH₄ + Cl₂ → CH₃Cl + HCl (in sunlight); further substitution can occur
This is called a substitution reaction (or halogenation/chlorination)

sub_questions.solution: When chlorine (Cl₂) reacts with methane (CH₄) in the presence of sunlight, a hydrogen atom in methane is replaced by a chlorine atom to form chloromethane (CH₃Cl) and hydrogen chloride (HCl). The reaction is: CH₄ + Cl₂ →(sunlight) CH₃Cl + HCl. The reaction can proceed further with more Cl₂ to produce CH₂Cl₂, CHCl₃, and CCl₄. This type of reaction is called a substitution reaction (specifically, a photochemical halogenation or chlorination reaction), as one atom in the reactant is substituted by another atom.

Acidified potassium dichromate (K₂Cr₂O₇)

sub_questions.solution: The two oxidising agents used for the conversion of alcohols to carboxylic acids are: (1) Alkaline potassium permanganate (KMnO₄) — it oxidises ethanol (CH₃CH₂OH) to acetic acid (CH₃COOH). (2) Acidified potassium dichromate (K₂Cr₂O₇) — it also acts as an oxidising agent to convert alcohols to the corresponding carboxylic acids. For example: CH₃CH₂OH + [O] → CH₃COOH (using either reagent).

sub_questions.text: (iv) सहसंयोजी यौगिकों और आयनिक यौगिकों के गुणों के बीच चार अन्तरों की सूची बनाइए।
sub_questions.text_english: (iv) List four differences in properties between covalent compounds and ionic compounds.

key_points: Melting/boiling points: covalent compounds have low; ionic compounds have high
Solubility: covalent compounds are generally insoluble in water; ionic compounds are generally soluble in water
Electrical conductivity: covalent compounds are poor conductors; ionic compounds conduct electricity in molten/aqueous state
State at room temperature: covalent compounds are mostly liquids or gases; ionic compounds are solid crystalline substances

sub_questions.solution: Four differences between covalent and ionic compounds: (1) Melting and Boiling Points — Covalent compounds have low melting and boiling points because they have weak intermolecular forces, whereas ionic compounds have high melting and boiling points due to strong electrostatic forces between ions. (2) Solubility — Most covalent compounds are insoluble in water but soluble in organic solvents; ionic compounds are generally highly soluble in water. (3) Electrical Conductivity — Covalent compounds are poor conductors of electricity as they do not have free ions; ionic compounds conduct electricity in molten state or aqueous solution due to free mobile ions. (4) Physical State — Covalent compounds are usually liquids or gases at room temperature; ionic compounds are generally hard, brittle solids at room temperature.

sub_questions.text: (i) कारण दीजिए कि कार्बन मुख्यतः सहसंयोजी आबन्ध द्वारा ही यौगिक क्यों बनाता है।
sub_questions.text_english: (i) Give reason why carbon forms compounds mainly by covalent bonding.

key_points: Carbon has 4 valence electrons — it can neither lose all 4 (too much energy needed) nor gain 4 (highly electronegative element would not accept all 4)
So carbon shares its 4 valence electrons with other atoms to form 4 covalent bonds

sub_questions.solution: Carbon has 4 valence electrons and needs 4 more to complete its octet. It cannot easily lose all 4 electrons to form a C⁴⁺ ion because that would require an enormous amount of energy. It also cannot gain 4 electrons from other atoms to form C⁴⁻ because it would be difficult for 6 protons in the nucleus to hold 10 electrons. Therefore, carbon achieves a stable octet configuration by sharing its 4 valence electrons with other atoms, forming four strong covalent bonds. This is why carbon predominantly forms covalent compounds.

sub_questions.text: (ii) सहसंयोजी यौगिकों के गलनांक और क्वथनांक निम्न क्यों होते हैं?
sub_questions.text_english: (ii) Why do covalent compounds have low melting and boiling points?

key_points: Covalent compounds are made up of discrete molecules held together by weak intermolecular forces (van der Waals forces)
Only small amounts of energy are needed to overcome these weak forces, hence low melting and boiling points

sub_questions.solution: Covalent compounds have low melting and boiling points because they consist of discrete molecules held together by weak intermolecular forces (such as van der Waals forces). These weak forces require only a small amount of energy to be overcome. In contrast, ionic compounds have strong electrostatic forces of attraction between oppositely charged ions, requiring much more energy to break. Therefore, covalent compounds melt and boil at relatively low temperatures.

sub_questions.text: (iii) निम्नलिखित के लिए कारण दीजिए: I. सहसंयोजी यौगिक विद्युत के कुचालक होते हैं। II. कार्बन श्रृंखलन दर्शाता है।
sub_questions.text_english: (iii) Give reason for the following: I. Covalent compounds are bad conductors of electricity. II. Carbon shows catenation.

key_points: I. Covalent compounds do not have free ions or electrons; charge cannot flow through them
II. Carbon forms strong C-C bonds with itself; it can form long chains, branches, and rings due to its small size and tetravalency

sub_questions.solution: I. Covalent compounds are bad conductors of electricity because they are made up of neutral molecules. When dissolved in water or melted, they do not form free ions. Since there are no freely mobile charged particles (ions or electrons) to carry electric current, covalent compounds cannot conduct electricity. II. Carbon shows catenation because the carbon-carbon (C–C) covalent bond is very strong and stable. Carbon atoms can bond with each other to form long chains, branched chains, and even ring structures. Carbon's small atomic size and tetravalency (4 valence electrons) allow it to form multiple stable bonds with other carbon atoms, resulting in a vast number of organic compounds.

sub_questions.text_english: (b) What should be the current rating of the electric circuit (220 V) so that an electric iron of 1 kW power rating can be operated?

sub_questions.solution: Given: Power P = 1 kW = 1000 W, Voltage V = 220 V. Using the formula P = VI, the current I = P/V = 1000/220 ≈ 4.55 A. Therefore, the electric circuit should have a current rating of at least 5 A to safely operate the 1 kW electric iron.

sub_questions.text_english: (c)(i) What is the function of the earth wire? State the advantage of the earth wire in domestic electric appliances such as electric iron.

key_points: Earth wire provides a low-resistance path to the ground for any leakage current
If the live wire accidentally touches the metal casing of the appliance, the current flows to earth through the earth wire instead of through the user's body, preventing electric shock

sub_questions.solution: The function of the earth wire is to provide a safety path for any leakage of electric current. It connects the metal body/casing of electrical appliances directly to the earth (ground). In domestic appliances like an electric iron, if due to a fault the live wire comes in contact with the metallic body of the iron, the leakage current immediately flows through the low-resistance earth wire to the ground. This prevents the current from flowing through the user's body when they touch the appliance, thus protecting them from a potentially fatal electric shock. The earth wire thus acts as a safety device.

sub_questions.text: (ग)(ii) विद्युत से होने वाली दुर्घटनाओं से बचाव के लिए ली जाने वाली दो सावधानियों की सूची बनाइए। उल्लेख कीजिए कि ये सावधानियाँ किस प्रकार परिपथ/साधित्र को संभावित क्षति से बचाती हैं।
sub_questions.text_english: (c)(ii) List two precautions to be taken to avoid electrical accidents. State how these precautions prevent possible damage to the circuit/appliance.

key_points: Precaution 1: Use of fuse/MCB — when current exceeds safe limit, fuse wire melts (or MCB trips), breaking the circuit and preventing overheating/fire
Precaution 2: Earthing of appliances — leakage current flows to earth safely, protecting both the user and the appliance from damage

sub_questions.solution: Two precautions to avoid electrical accidents are: (1) Use of Fuse or MCB (Miniature Circuit Breaker) — A fuse contains a thin wire of low melting point. When excessive current flows through the circuit, the fuse wire melts and breaks the circuit, preventing overheating of wires and possible fire. An MCB automatically trips when current exceeds the rated value, protecting both the circuit and connected appliances from damage due to short circuits or overloads. (2) Earthing (Grounding) of appliances — All metallic body appliances must be properly earthed. If a fault causes the live wire to touch the metal casing, the leakage current is directed safely to the ground through the earth wire, preventing electric shock to the user and protecting the appliance from further damage.

sub_questions.solution: When brine (concentrated aqueous solution of sodium chloride) is electrolysed, the following products are formed: chlorine gas at the anode, hydrogen gas at the cathode, and sodium hydroxide solution. The balanced chemical equation is: 2NaCl(aq) + 2H₂O(l) → 2NaOH(aq) + Cl₂(g) + H₂(g). This process is known as the Chlor-Alkali process.

key_points: Chlorine: used in water purification/disinfection; used in manufacturing of PVC, CFCs, and pesticides; used as bleaching agent
OR Sodium hydroxide: used in making soap and detergents; used in paper manufacturing; used in degreasing metals

sub_questions.solution: Two uses of chlorine (a product of electrolysis of brine): (1) Chlorine is used for disinfecting and purifying drinking water and swimming pools by killing harmful microorganisms. (2) Chlorine is used in the manufacture of bleaching powder, PVC (polyvinyl chloride), pesticides, and various chemicals used in industry. Alternatively, sodium hydroxide (NaOH) is used in making soaps and detergents, and in the paper and pulp industry.

sub_questions.text: (ग)(i) किसी दुर्बल असंक्षारक क्षारीय लवण 'A' का उपयोग खाने को शीघ्रता से पकाने में किया जाता है। इसे गरम करने पर कोई यौगिक 'B' बनता है जिसका उपयोग जल की स्थायी कठोरता को दूर करने में किया जाता है। A और B को पहचानिए तथा A को गरम करने पर होने वाली अभिक्रिया का समीकरण भी लिखिए।
sub_questions.text_english: (c)(i) A mild non-corrosive basic salt 'A', used for faster cooking, is strongly heated to produce a compound 'B', that is used for removing permanent hardness of water. Identify A and B and also write the equation for the reaction that occurs when A is heated.

key_points: A = Sodium bicarbonate (baking soda) — NaHCO₃; used in pressure cookers/cooking
B = Sodium carbonate (washing soda) — Na₂CO₃; used to remove permanent hardness of water
Equation: 2NaHCO₃ → Na₂CO₃ + H₂O + CO₂

sub_questions.solution: Salt A is Sodium bicarbonate (NaHCO₃), commonly known as baking soda. It is a mild, non-corrosive basic salt used in cooking to make food cook faster (used in pressure cookers and as a leavening agent). When strongly heated, sodium bicarbonate decomposes to form Compound B, which is Sodium carbonate (Na₂CO₃), commonly called washing soda. Sodium carbonate is used to remove the permanent hardness of water by precipitating calcium and magnesium ions. The equation for the reaction when A is heated is: 2NaHCO₃ →(heat) Na₂CO₃ + H₂O + CO₂↑.

sub_questions.text: (ग)(ii) क्रिस्टलन के जल की परिभाषा लिखिए। उन दो लवणों का उदाहरण दीजिए जिनमें क्रिस्टलन का जल होता है।
sub_questions.text_english: (c)(ii) Define water of crystallisation. Give two examples of salts that have water of crystallisation.

key_points: Water of crystallisation is the fixed number of water molecules that are chemically bonded within the crystal structure of a salt
Example 1: Copper sulphate pentahydrate — CuSO₄·5H₂O (blue vitriol)
Example 2: Sodium carbonate decahydrate — Na₂CO₃·10H₂O (washing soda)

sub_questions.solution: Water of crystallisation is defined as the fixed number of water molecules that are chemically incorporated and held within the crystal lattice of a crystalline salt. The presence of water of crystallisation gives the salt its definite crystalline shape and, in many cases, its characteristic colour. Two examples of salts containing water of crystallisation are: (1) Copper sulphate pentahydrate — CuSO₄·5H₂O, commonly known as blue vitriol, which has 5 water molecules per formula unit and appears blue in colour. (2) Sodium carbonate decahydrate — Na₂CO₃·10H₂O, commonly known as washing soda, which has 10 water molecules per formula unit.

questions.text: सभी जीवों का अनुरक्षण कार्य निरन्तर होना चाहिए। यह उस समय भी चलते रहना चाहिए जब वे कोई विशेष काम नहीं कर रहे होते हैं। जब हम सो रहे हों अथवा अपनी कक्षा में बैठे होते हैं, उस समय भी यह अनुरक्षण का काम चलता रहना चाहिए। कोशिकाओं और ऊतकों की क्षति और टूट-फूट को रोकने तथा अनुरक्षण प्रक्रियाओं के लिए ऊर्जा की आवश्यकता होती है। यह ऊर्जा एकल जीव के शरीर को स्वपोषियों, जिन्हें उत्पादक कहते हैं, से प्राप्त होती है।
questions.text_english: The maintenance functions of all living organisms must go on even when they are not doing anything particular. Even when we are just sitting in a class or even asleep, this maintenance job has to go on. These maintenance processes require energy to prevent damage and break-down of cells and tissues, which is obtained by the individual organism from the food prepared by the autotrophs, called producers.

sub_questions.text: (क) उस प्रक्रिया का नाम और परिभाषा लिखिए जिसके द्वारा हरे पादप भोजन निर्मित करते हैं।
sub_questions.text_english: (a) Name and define the process by which green plants prepare food.

key_points: Process: Photosynthesis
Definition: The process by which green plants use sunlight, water, and carbon dioxide to synthesise glucose (food) and release oxygen

sub_questions.solution: The process is called Photosynthesis. It is defined as the process by which green plants (autotrophs) use sunlight energy absorbed by chlorophyll to convert carbon dioxide (from air) and water (from soil) into glucose (food/chemical energy) and release oxygen as a by-product. It occurs in the chloroplasts of plant cells.

sub_questions.text: (ख) उपर्युक्त प्रक्रिया में होने वाली अभिक्रिया का रासायनिक समीकरण लिखिए।
sub_questions.text_english: (b) Write chemical equation involved in the above process.

key_points: 6CO₂ + 6H₂O →(sunlight, chlorophyll) C₆H₁₂O₆ + 6O₂

sub_questions.solution: The chemical equation for photosynthesis is: 6CO₂ + 6H₂O →(sunlight + chlorophyll) C₆H₁₂O₆ + 6O₂. Six molecules of carbon dioxide combine with six molecules of water in the presence of sunlight and chlorophyll to produce one molecule of glucose (C₆H₁₂O₆) and six molecules of oxygen.

sub_questions.text: (ग)(i) मरुद्भिद (मरुस्थली) पौधों द्वारा भोजन के संश्लेषण के समय होने वाली घटनाओं का उचित अनुक्रम में उल्लेख कीजिए।
sub_questions.text_english: (c)(i) State in proper sequence the events that occur in synthesis of food by desert plants.

key_points: Desert plants (CAM plants) open stomata only at night to take in CO₂ and store it as organic acids (malic acid)
During the day, stomata remain closed to prevent water loss
Stored CO₂ is released during the day and used for the light-dependent reactions of photosynthesis using sunlight

sub_questions.solution: Desert plants (such as cacti) use a special type of photosynthesis called CAM (Crassulacean Acid Metabolism) to conserve water. The sequence of events is: (1) At night, desert plants open their stomata to absorb carbon dioxide (CO₂) from the atmosphere. (2) The absorbed CO₂ is converted and stored as malic acid (an organic acid) in vacuoles to prevent water loss during the hot daytime. (3) During the day, the stomata remain closed to minimise transpiration and water loss. (4) The stored malic acid is broken down during the day to release CO₂. (5) This released CO₂ is then used in the light-dependent reactions of photosynthesis using sunlight energy, to produce glucose.

sub_questions.text: (ग)(ii) कारण सहित व्याख्या कीजिए कि (I) घटा वाले (मेघाच्छन्न) मौसम में, तथा (II) धूल द्वारा रंध्रों को बंद कर दिए जाने पर हरे पादपों द्वारा भोजन निर्माण करने की दर पर क्या प्रभाव पड़ता है।
sub_questions.text_english: (c)(ii) Explain giving reasons what happens to the rate at which the green plants will prepare food (I) during cloudy weather, and (II) when stomata get blocked due to dust.

key_points: (I) Cloudy weather: rate of photosynthesis decreases because sunlight (a raw material) is reduced; light reactions cannot proceed at full capacity
(II) Stomata blocked by dust: rate of photosynthesis decreases because CO₂ cannot enter the leaves through stomata; also, O₂ cannot be released, further inhibiting the process

sub_questions.solution: (I) During cloudy weather: The rate of photosynthesis decreases significantly. Sunlight is one of the essential raw materials for photosynthesis (required for the light-dependent reactions in which water is split and ATP/NADPH are produced). When the sky is overcast, the intensity of sunlight reaching the leaves is greatly reduced. As a result, the light reactions slow down, less ATP and NADPH are produced, and therefore the overall rate of glucose synthesis (food preparation) by the green plants decreases. (II) When stomata get blocked due to dust: The rate of photosynthesis also decreases. Stomata are the tiny pores on the surface of leaves through which carbon dioxide (CO₂) enters and oxygen (O₂) is released. When dust particles block the stomata, CO₂ cannot enter the leaf cells. Since CO₂ is a raw material for the dark reactions (Calvin cycle) of photosynthesis, its reduced availability leads to a lower rate of food (glucose) synthesis in the plant.
